clue.text: Cancellation of credit results in reprimand

parts.note: a tick is credit, as in buying something on tick
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A bank withdrawing someone's credit triggers a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is an informal idiom for scolding or rebuking someone.

clue.text: Ground coach without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the coach word surrounds the hesitation

parts.note: to coach is to train
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A trainer drives the team over the land, never pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: TRAIN goes around ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Trainee accountant got up to make hay

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the word reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: to ted is to spread grass out to dry as hay

explanation.surface: A junior accountant rose early to bring in the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a farming verb, to turn and spread mown grass; 'got up' reverses it to DET in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person in training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Appeal to analyse verse in an ancient language

parts.note: O is an appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'
to scan is to analyse the metre of verse

explanation.surface: A request to study poetry in a dead tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an Italic tongue of ancient southern Italy, related to Latin.

clue.text: Chance to impound equipment from naval vessel

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: fate is chance or fortune
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An opportunity to seize gear from a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a warship, historically a fast sailing ship and now an escort vessel.

clue.text: Treasury employs tender-hearted surveyor

indicators.note: with tender as its heart, one word sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for chartered surveyor
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: The government's finance department hires a kindly man to survey land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts OFFER (tender) as the heart of CS, the abbreviation for a chartered surveyor.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are the funds or strongboxes of a state or organisation, its treasury.

clue.text: Association needs to study diplomacy

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people

explanation.surface: Relations between nations require learning the art of negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact is connection or communication between people, an association.

clue.text: Understand that the calculation is wrong

parts.note: a figure is a calculated number
out means wrong, as in 'out in one's reckoning'

explanation.surface: Realise that the sum has an error in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure out is an idiom for working out or comprehending.

clue.text: Four entered to assassinate senior manager

indicators.note: four entered the other word, going inside it

parts.note: to execute is to put to death
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four men broke in to murder the company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a person with senior managerial responsibility in a business.

clue.text: Spare soft-headed man making advances

indicators.note: headed takes just the head, the opening letter, of soft

parts.note: a lender advances money

explanation.surface: A thin, foolish fellow keeps making passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft-headed' looks like 'foolish' but gives the head of soft, S; the advances are loans, not passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean lean or thin, as a slim build is.

clue.text: Introduce changes, but fewer of them

indicators.note: the word introduce undergoes changes, its letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to bring in reforms, only not so many of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in number means having fewer of something.

clue.text: Land bought initially in great delight

indicators.note: the first letter of bought is placed in the word for great delight

parts.note: glee is great delight

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of bought

explanation.surface: Someone buys a plot and is overjoyed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: GLEBE is land assigned to a parish priest as part of his living.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is church land, a portion of ground given to a clergyman's benefice.

clue.text: Aerial acquired before Miss Widdecombe returned

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

indicators.note: returned means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann Widdecombe is a former British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An aerial was bought before the politician Ann Widdecombe came back.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Widdecombe is a former British Conservative MP and TV personality; 'returned' turns ANN to NNA. 'acquired' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a rod or wire for receiving radio signals, an aerial.

clue.text: Silver ring found in shallow water

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a ring or circle

explanation.surface: A silver ring is discovered in the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground has touched bottom in water too shallow to float.

clue.text: Nigel replaced a man foe being remiss

indicators.note: the letters of Nigel are replaced, put back in a new order

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Nigel was swapped out for another man because he was slack.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned 'foe' should read 'for', a link. 'replaced' rearranges NIGEL to NEGLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless or lax in one's duty, as someone remiss is.

clue.text: Dying on the California trail

explanation.definitionFit: Going west is slang for perishing, and literally heading westward as pioneers did to California.

clue.text: She went in disguise when making headlines

indicators.note: in disguise means the words appear in altered form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman sneaks in incognito while she is famous in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the news means being reported on, featuring in headlines.

clue.text: A bit of a basket-case

parts.note: read literally, a piece of a basket: a willow twig of the kind woven into wickerwork

explanation.definitionFit: Osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Swallow fast

explanation.definitionFit: A swift is a bird much like a swallow, and swift also means quick.

clue.text: Secretly in Rome

parts.note: the Latin phrase, as a Roman would say 'in confidence'

explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa is Latin, literally under the rose, meaning in confidence.

clue.text: Anxious admission by a hospital inmate

parts.note: I'm (I am) is an admission, a confession of what one is
a patient is someone being treated in hospital

explanation.surface: Someone in a hospital ward confesses to being nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The inmate's admission is 'I'm patient', ironic since the answer means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means restless and eager, unable to wait calmly.

clue.text: If sick people understand nothing, it's a bad sign

indicators.note: split as under-stand: in this down clue the people stand under the nothing

parts.note: ill means sick
O is the figure zero, nothing
men are people

explanation.surface: If unwell folk are baffled, the omens are poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understand' is read as 'stand under': MEN comes below O in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill omen is a portent of misfortune, a bad sign.

clue.text: Tenor serves unadulterated French wine

parts.note: pur is French for pure
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A singer pours out pure French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' is not the singer but the gist or meaning of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Purport is the general meaning or drift of something, its tenor.

clue.text: Hill split asunder by violent flood

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
rent means torn apart

explanation.surface: A hillside is torn open by a raging deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a rushing, violent stream of water.

clue.text: A large quantity doesn't impress me!

explanation.definitionFit: A big deal is a great amount, and the dismissive exclamation 'big deal!' means 'so what?'.

clue.text: Either way, it's a tonic

indicators.note: either way means the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, this drink picks you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviver is a restorative drink or medicine, something that perks you up like a tonic.

clue.text: Caller without it may squint in the sun!

definitions.text: Caller without it may squint in the sun!

indicators.note: without means the word it is removed from the caller

parts.note: a caller is a visitor

explanation.surface: A visitor lacking something squints in bright sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue says anyone lacking this peaked shade will squint.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a shade worn over the eyes against glare.

clue.text: Utter depravity envelops oriental leader

indicators.note: envelops means one word wraps round another

parts.note: vice is depravity, wickedness

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of oriental

explanation.surface: Absolute wickedness surrounds an Eastern chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (total) but is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to express it in words, to say it.

clue.text: Some seem to be seriously overweight

indicators.note: some indicates only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Certain people appear dangerously heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, very fat.

clue.text: Light in the darkness? Nonsense!

explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is moonlight shining at night, and also foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Sinatra became expert at his trade

indicators.note: the name Sinatra became something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra developed into a master of his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled craftsman working with his hands.

clue.text: Suffering endured by old marines under canvas

indicators.note: the inner pieces are endured, held, by the outer word

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Veteran marines put up with hardship while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endured by' puts O and RM (Royal Marines, the British naval infantry) inside TENT; 'under canvas' reads as camping.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe physical or mental pain, great suffering.
